predecessors.name: Sultanate of Oman
predecessors.text: the interior of Oman, 'north to Ibri and south to the Alsharqiyah region and the Sharqiya Sands', between the Hajar Mountains and the Rub' al Khali, which seceded from the Sultan at Muscat in 1913

successors.name: Sultanate of Oman
successors.text: the interior, taken over in January 1959: 'With the defeat of the Imam, the Treaty of Seeb was terminated and the autonomous Imamate of Oman was abolished'

ledger.x: 1913: Imam Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi revives the Imamate of Oman at Nizwa and rebels against Muscat.
1913: the interior passes from Muscat to the Imamate.
1913: the rebellion against the Sultan begins and runs to 1920.
1920: the Treaty of Seeb ends the rebellion.
25 September 1920: the Imamate accepts the Sultan's sovereignty with autonomy.
25 October 1954: the autonomy ends in breach of the treaty.
25 October 1954: the Muscat Infantry occupy Fahud and the Jebel Akhdar War begins.
1957: the rising frees the Nizwa district.
30 January 1959: the Jebel Akhdar War ends in the Sultan's victory.
January 1959: the Imamate of Oman is abolished.

wars.name: Omani Imamate rebellion
wars.outcome: The Imamate held the interior against the Sultan; the Treaty of Seeb (25 September 1920) left it autonomous under the Sultan's sovereignty, a 'de facto split between Oman and Muscat'.

wars.name: Jebel Akhdar War
wars.outcome: The Sultan, with direct British support (RAF raids from July 1958, the SAS on the plateau on 30 January 1959), defeats the Imamate: Nizwa falls on 15 December 1955, the 1957 rising frees the Nizwa district again and the Treaty of Seeb is terminated and the…

certainty.note: The Hajar Mountains and the Rub' al Khali are natural limits, not surveyed lines; the Treaty of Seeb gives no boundary, only autonomy for 'the interior of Oman'; no page gives a frontier change in 1920-1959, and the fighting of 1954-1959…
